_about: The World Shipping Council's Top 50 Container Ports, ranked on 2024 statistics (https://www.worldshipping.org/top-50-container-ports). The WSC page draws its table with a script and could not be read from the sandbox this was built in, so the ranks and names are as two full reproductions of that table give them, which agree row for row: Goliath Africa Logistics, 'TOP 50 Container Ports in the World', 12 Feb 2026 (https://www.goliath-africa.com/top-50-container-ports-in-the-world/), and PortNews24, 'Top 50 Container Ports by Throughput: 2026 Global Ranking', 30 Jul 2026 (https://portnews24.com/article/top-50-container-ports-by-throughput). The WSC page now says it ranks on 2025 statistics. `codes`: the port's standard UN/LOCODE first, then the other codes in common use for it (a port system's port areas, the WPI's own code). Every code must resolve in web/public/map/ports.json and engine/data/ports.tsv (tests/test_places.py, web/tests/unit/lib.test.ts). `left_out`: codes in common use that neither the World Port Index nor the UN/LOCODE code list can place (no WPI row, no coordinates); they stay unplaced, and the confirm screen names them. Fetched 2026-11-27. A list of facts used as test data only; nothing here ships.
source: World Shipping Council, Top 50 Container Ports (2024 statistics)

left_out.why: Manzanillo International Terminal: no WPI row, and the UN/LOCODE entry has no coordinates
Yangshan: no WPI row, no UN/LOCODE coordinates; the WPI's Shanghai row is the river port, about 70 km away
Waigaoqiao: no WPI row, no UN/LOCODE coordinates
